amendments.reason: The registered eager/compiled equivalence check FAILED on the final-bpb criterion (0.326% vs 0.3%; loss criterion passed 0.33% vs 0.5%), so per the launch plan the tranche uses the eager reference profile (65,194 tok/s, ~1.005 s/update, half the compiled speed). At 250M targets (3,814 updates) the eager tranche needs ~85 min (~$2.54), exceeding the 1.4 h runtime limit and the $2.40 hard cap. 2,000 updates (131,072,000 targets, a checkpoint boundary) gives ~61 min (~$1.81) with the measured overheads (process start, canary, replica waits, 27 s evals, checkpoints), ~10 min below the $2.10 soft limit. validation_scored_bytes corrected to the v0.2.2 value (field unused by the tooling; the manifest takes it from validation_record.json).

amendments.reason: Independent review of the launch chain (findings T-01, T-10, T-13, T-15): the readiness matrix was not bound to the gate-definition file, so a matrix evaluated from a trimmed gate set (the committed 16-gate matrix predates B17) could authorize a launch; the policy now names the base gate ids every authorizing matrix must contain (B13 split into B13a timing / B13b shutdown drills / B13c funding, plus B17 startup qualification). The reviewed 900 s stall rule, the 90 % canary throughput allowance and the volume paths both supervisors must target were constants in code or prose; they are registered here so launch_guard.py compares the armed controllers and the canary against the policy instead of literals. No limit, schedule, seed, LR, cadence or acceptance threshold changes.

Launch limits amended under funding contract v5 (LAUNCH allocation hard 3.50 / soft 3.00, 1.8 h) using the measured all-in eager cost (65,194 tok/s reference; 2,000 updates about 34 min of updates plus startup, evaluations, checkpoints and replica waits); the training scope stays 2,000 updates / 131,072,000 targets. amendments.reason: Owner continuation decision after the limited tranche (report launch_r2_report.md: 1.2228 bpb at 2,000; canary C1-C9 accepted; all six checkpoints preserved). The remaining 50,034 updates at the measured 1.00 s/update (13.9 h) plus the measured evaluation/checkpoint overhead (27.3 s per 500-update cycle in the r2 tranche: ~0.8 h) and startup need about 14.8 h, about $28.1 at the declared $1.90/h session rate ($1.79 GPU + $0.028 disk observed); the limits carry a margin (soft 30.0 / hard 33.0 / 17.5 h) inside funding contract v7. The tranche stop becomes the full horizon (a continuation may end at the horizon; a fresh run still needs a strict prefix). Every-500-update checkpoints (100 x 1.63 GiB) exceed the 50 GB volume and the HDD, so retention keeps every 10th off-site as the owner chose (13 keepers: 0, 2000, 5000..50000, 52034). Canary rule unchanged: the continuation reuses the accepted canary of this run (its acceptance record is bound by hash) and resumes from exactly the declared verified checkpoint; a newer valid checkpoint on the volume stops the runner for an operator decision.

retention.volume: the launch guard deletes non-keepers once their HDD replica is verified, always keeping the two newest valid checkpoints; keepers stay on the volume until the run ends
retention.hdd: the replicator deletes non-keepers after a newer verified replica (two newest kept); the preserver releases keepers after both off-site receipts, keeping the two newest preserved keepers
retention.offsite: keepers only (Drive + HF), each within preservation.offsite_deadline_seconds of its HDD verification
